2027 Alpine A290 Premiere Edition Heading to Japan in RHD, Only 100 Units on the Way
7 photos
Photo: Alpine / edited
Alpine has brought its first electric model to Japan, where prospective customers are presented with a limited availability problem. The launch specification, which is called A290 Premiere Edition, is capped at 100 examples. Nicely equipped from the outset, said B-segment electric hatchback carries a starting price of 6,490,000 yen, converting to nearly 40,600 dollars at current exchange rates.
Truth be told, Alpine 's urban dweller is expensive back home in France as well. The most affordable of the bunch is the 130-kW GT, which costs 34,670 euros in combination with the government's 4,830-euro Certificats d'Economies d'Energie bonus. Indeed, the French supermini is expensive in all configurations.
Alpine Japan's advertised price includes consumption tax, and the Premiere Edition is neatly split between two colors. Each features a front-mounted electric motor with 218 ps (215 hp) on tap, along with a 52-kWh battery pack. Alpine Japan has yet to confirm when less expensive versions will become available. For now, the well-equipped Premiere Edition will have to suffice in Japan.
Its available paint colors are called Blanc Nival and Blue Alpine Vision. Both are joined by a Noir Profond-painted roof, and both feature different brake caliper finishes. Blue cars receive blue calipers, naturally, while the white A290 Premiere Edition gets red ones. There is no such differentiation inside, where Alpine went for Deep Glue and Ever Grey Nappa leather upholstery throughout.
Customers who put money down between November 19, 2026, and March 31, 2026, receive 12 months of free Alpine Charging Card membership. Said charging card provides access to the e-Mobility Power charging network, and obviously, every kilowatt-hour consumed at those stations has to be paid by the customer.
Photo: Alpine Measuring a little over 4 meters from bumper to bumper, the angry-looking A290 Premiere Edition is a very small car. Alpine Japan lists 2,535 millimeters for the wheelbase, namely 99.8 inches in American speak. Its curb weight of 1,480 kilograms (3,263 pounds), however, is a reminder that electric vehicles are heavier than their internal combustion equivalents.
Capable of seating five, the Renault 5 E-Tech's fancier and sportier cousin is very different where it matters from the volume-oriented sibling. The suspension, chassis, and electronic controls are unique to the Alpine, which its maker developed from the outset to be the superior driving machine. Good for 300 Newton-meters (221 pound-feet) at full chatter, the A290 Premiere Edition hits 100 kph (62 mph) in 6.4 seconds.
Its high-voltage battery sits low under the floor, helping lower the center of gravity while also freeing up cabin space. Alpine Japan quotes no more than 360 kilometers (224 miles) in the WLTC test cycle, and the local division references data obtained by a French testing organization using a British-market vehicle. Only available in RHD, the Japanese model flaunts hydraulic compression stops at every corner to control suspension movement.
Brake Torque Vectoring for the Brembo performance brakes also needs highlighting, along with Michelin Pilot Sport S 5 rubber measuring 225/40 by 19 inches. Just like European models, the A290 Premiere Edition is rocking a red OV-marked button on the steering wheel. Press it, and the powertrain delivers max output for no more than 10 seconds.
A heated steering wheel, adaptive cruise control, heated front seats, rear brake support, and a 60:40 split-folding rear bench are on the menu as well. Every A290 Premiere Edition ships with a Devialet audio system that includes nine speakers, a sub, and a dedicated amp, delivering 615 watts. Said audio setup is used by the Alpine Drive Sound system to play synthetic electric soundscapes designed around its zero-emission powertrain.
